name: Alberta Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA)
summary: Alberta's private-sector privacy legislation, deemed substantially similar to PIPEDA by the federal government. It governs how private-sector organizations in Alberta collect, use, and disclose personal information, including employee personal information, and applies to provincially regulated organizations operating within the province.
keyRequirements: Obtain consent before collecting, using, or disclosing personal information
Collect only the personal information reasonably necessary for the stated purpose
Provide individuals access to their personal information and the right to request corrections
Protect personal information with reasonable security safeguards
Designate a privacy officer responsible for compliance

Notify the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta without unreasonable delay of any breach posing a real risk of significant harm; notify affected individuals when the Commissioner requires it
Collect, use, and disclose employee personal information only as reasonably required to establish, manage, or end the employment relationship
penalties: Fines up to $10,000 CAD for individuals and $100,000 CAD for organizations per offense, including for failing to notify the Commissioner of a breach. Enforced by the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta. No private right of action.
